candidates.evidence: Four measured peaks at 92.5, 162.4, 189.4 and 226.5 cm-1 (FWHM 3.2-8.2 cm-1). The strongest pair (162, 189) and the 92 and ~224 features match the Raman modes usually quoted for orthorhombic SnS (about 96 Ag, 163 B3g, 192 Ag, 218/224). Matching is from memory of the literature, not checked against a reference spectrum; positions differ by -3.5 to +2.5 cm-1, which is larger than the fit error.

Isostructural Pnma sibling with a similar A_g/B_3g mode set in the same window. Not verified against reference data here; Ge is lighter than Sn, so its modes would be expected at higher frequency, which weakens this candidate.

limits: Angle-resolved data: 18 angles (0-170 deg, 10 deg steps) in parallel and crossed configurations, 1 cm-1 step, 60-382 cm-1. Per-point noise about 140 counts on a background near 240 counts, so per-angle amplitude errors are about 450 (162 cm-1), 450-500 (93, 189) and 750 (226). Peak amplitudes were obtained by fitting Lorentzians with positions and widths fixed to the config-averaged parallel fit, with a linear background.

Cosmic-ray spikes: none found. A robust single-point excursion scan (6 sigma threshold) returned no hits, and all intensity maxima sit on multi-point peaks. Only the zero-valued dropout pixels were removed.
Window ends at 382 cm-1, so Si (520.7 cm-1) and higher-frequency SnS modes and second-order bands are not measured. The absence of Si is expected for a suspended sample but cannot be checked here.

Absolute frequency calibration is not verified (no standard lamp or Si reference in this window). Position uncertainties from the fit are about 0.03 cm-1 (statistical); a systematic offset of about 1-2 cm-1 is plausible.
Literature matching is from memory and was not verified. The residuals against the literature values (-3.5, -0.6, -2.6, +2.5 cm-1) are not a consistent offset, so the identification is tentative.

Polarization origin: the zero of the angle axis is unknown. Phases (fourfold maxima at about 18 deg, twofold maximum at about 61-65 deg) are relative to the stage zero, not to crystal axes, so they cannot fix the irrep assignments.
Ag (traceless diagonal) and B_3g modes both give fourfold patterns with a 45-degree offset in this backscattering geometry, so irrep labels for the 162 and 93 cm-1 modes are tentative.

Pattern for 226 cm-1 (twofold in parallel, crossed about zero) is not what a single diagonal Raman tensor gives in this geometry, so it may be a superposition or may reflect limited crossed-channel sensitivity. The 218/224 doublet is not resolved; a two-component fit is not favoured, but it cannot be excluded at this signal-to-noise.

Crossed-channel leakage: the crossed intensities of 189 and 226 are about 1.6-2% of parallel, consistent with zero but not strictly zero. The crossed/parallel ratio also assumes equal throughput for both configurations, which was not calibrated.
No second-order or weak modes above 3 sigma residual were found in the config-averaged fit. Weak features near 107-150 cm-1 are at the noise level and were not claimed.

Layer number, thickness, stacking, and stoichiometry cannot be determined from these data. Temperature (295 K) is given in the metadata and was not verified by a Stokes/anti-Stokes or peak-width analysis.
